content: {"summary":"During the 15 May 2025 incident the catalog‑api pods ran with an async worker setup and a SQLAlchemy connection pool limited to 30 sessions. A traffic pattern of roughly 65 requests per second quickly exhausted the pool, causing QueuePool timeouts and resulting in 504 errors from the edge gateway.","likely_cause":"Connection‑pool exhaustion caused by a limited pool size (10 + 5 overflow) combined with high request rate after the May 2025 deployment","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"The catalog‑api pods used an async worker setup with a SQLAlchemy pool limited to 10 connections plus 5 overflow (max 30 sessions).","evidence_ids":["RB-028#1"],"quote":"SQLAlchemy pool allows 10 connections plus 5 overflow, so at most 30 sessions"},{"text":"Around 65 requests per second drained the pool almost immediately, leading the pods to log QueuePool timeouts at 14:02:30.","evidence_ids":["INC-0042#1"],"quote":"pool drained almost immediately. catalog-api-01 and catalog-api-02 began logging QueuePool timeouts"},{"text":"The edge gateway began answering 504 errors during the incident as a symptom of the slowdown.","evidence_ids":["INC-0042#0"],"quote":"edge-gateway began answering 504 during the incident"}],"next_checks":["Confirm whether the May 2025 deployment changed the SQLAlchemy pool configuration or increased async worker concurrency","Examine cache‑miss rates before and after the deployment to see if they rose sharply","Review deployment changelog for any modifications to connection‑pool or worker settings"]}
